09.label: See the types
09.heading:
Types in a
real table
09.caption: Every column declares its type — the database enforces it.

10.label: Missing data
10.heading:
NULL in a
users table
10.caption: Bob has no phone. Charlie has neither — both are NULL, not empty strings.

11.label: Conditions
11.heading:
Filters with
AND / OR / NOT
11.caption: WHERE age >= 18 AND country = 'IN' → returns Alice, Carol, Dan.

12.label: Filter lists
12.heading:
IN & BETWEEN
on orders
12.caption: WHERE region IN ('APAC','EU') AND amount BETWEEN 1000 AND 10000 → rows 102, 104.

13.label: Search data
13.heading:
LIKE on
user names
13.caption: WHERE name LIKE '%rahul%' → rows 1 & 3. WHERE name LIKE '_a_' → rows 2 & 4.

15.label: Group data
15.heading:
Users per
country
15.caption: GROUP BY country → one row per country. HAVING COUNT(*) > 50 → IN, US only.

16.label: Related tables
16.heading:
Orders +
customers
16.caption: INNER JOIN links orders.customer_id → customers.id. Only matching rows appear.

17.label: Keep left rows
17.heading:
Users with
or without orders
17.caption: LEFT JOIN keeps Bob even with no orders — his order columns are NULL.

18.label: Three tables
18.heading:
Orders + customer
+ product
18.caption: Two JOINs chain three tables. Aliases (o, c, p) keep it readable.

19.label: Nested queries
19.heading:
Find users
who ordered
19.caption: WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders) — only users with orders appear.

20.label: Stack results
20.heading:
Customers +
employees
20.caption: UNION merges both lists and removes duplicates. UNION ALL keeps every row.

21.label: Clean output
21.heading:
Before vs
after aliases
21.caption: Aliases rename output columns — reports read like plain English.

22.label: Conditional labels
22.heading:
Scores to
grades
22.caption: CASE WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A' … ELSE 'F' END — labels computed in SQL.

23.label: Time data
23.heading:
Orders with
dates
23.caption: DATE_FORMAT(created_at, '%Y-%m') → group orders by month for reports.

24.label: Text data
24.heading:
Names to
clean
24.caption: CONCAT(first, ' ', last) AS full_name — clean display names from parts.

25.label: Rankings
25.heading:
Students
ranked
25.caption: ROW_NUMBER() keeps every row and adds a rank — no data collapsed.

26.label: Named steps
26.heading:
Top users
defined
26.caption: WITH top_users AS (…points > 1000) → the main query reads it like a table.

27.label: Reusable query
27.heading:
Active users
view
27.caption: CREATE VIEW active_users AS SELECT … WHERE active = TRUE — query it anytime.

28.label: Lookup speed
28.heading:
Searching by
email
28.caption: CREATE INDEX on email → WHERE email = '…' finds rows instantly, no full scan.

29.label: Money movement
29.heading:
Bank
transfer
29.caption: BEGIN → two UPDATEs → COMMIT. Both happen or neither — data stays consistent.

30.label: Final build
30.heading:
E-commerce
tables
30.caption: Four tables, real relationships — everything you learned in 30 days.
